Here's a fun story about unreliable drug tests, specifically piss tests.

I work at an animal hospital emergency room. We routinely have dogs come in shaking, unsteady, glassy-eyed, pissing themselves - clearly marijuana toxicity. Dogs love the stuff for some reason and eat it all the time. We're so good at spotting pot tox that we don't even need to piss test the dogs, but we do anyways because we're an official medical facility and we need to document everything.

I'd say about 20% of the time, we get a good, clear positive. The other 80% of the time are partial-positives, or a straight up negative, even though the dog's owner has stated that yes, there is pot in the house and yes, the dog could have eaten it. Furthermore, we often get positives for drugs the dog clearly hasn't ingested.

Here is the specific piss test we use. This particular dog had eaten crystal meth. Notice how confusing the test is as well - a LINE means NEGATIVE, and NO LINE means POSITIVE ("non-negative"). So good, we have no line next to AMP (amphetamines), so he's positive for ice. But is that a line next to THC? Or is that no line? He's clearly negative for cocaine and opiates, but false positive for THC? Maybe. Who knows! We treated the dog for amphetamine ingestion and just shrugged about the THC.

Piss tests work the same for humans and dogs, it's all mammal urine so it all functions the same. If we get 20% clear positives for dogs, and our staff of trained medical personnel is still sometimes confused about how to read the test, what does that say about Shaniqua Beyonce Jackson who gets paid $9/hr to administer this piss test to alleged DWI arrests at the local police station in Harlem?
